Glorb · blend shape reference

The Ten Mouths

Every mouth position the viseme rig can drive, rendered on the Character Creator base mesh that is already talking. Sculpt against these, or keep the shapes that make them.

Keep the CC shapes. Don’t sculpt.

Your character came off the same Character Creator rig as this base mesh, so it already ships every shape below — and the code already finds them by name, reports Character Creator in the console, and drives them. Sculpting the eight is the fallback for a mesh that has none, not the goal.

The only thing that would force a sculpt is having already deleted these in your slimming pass. Check before you decide: load the export in face-test.html and read the status line. If it says mapped via Character Creator, there is nothing to sculpt.

The thirteen to keep

  • V_Open
  • V_Lip_Open
  • V_Wide
  • V_Tight_O
  • V_Tight
  • V_Dental_Lip
  • V_Explosive
  • V_Affricate
  • Mouth_Close
  • Mouth_Press_L
  • Mouth_Press_R
  • V_Tongue_Raise
  • V_Tongue_Out

Plus the CC_Base_JawRoot bone, which does the actual opening — Jaw_Open as a shape moves nearly five thousand vertices and barely parts the lips. Keep the tongue mesh too, or L has nothing to raise.

Open vowels

The jaw does the work; the shapes trim the lips.

Rounded

Protrusion is the read. Sculpt the lips forward, not merely narrow.

Lip contact

The lips actually meet. Under-sculpt these and he mumbles.

Tongue

Needs the tongue mesh to survive the export.

Everything else

One shape covering most consonants.

Neutral

Exporting it

  1. No Draco. The orb has its own GLB reader for the particle positions and it knows nothing about compression — a Draco file loads fine in the test page and fails in the app. Export uncompressed, or run it through tools/make_head.html, which also trims to the neck and drops the teeth.
  2. Keep the eye bones even if you drop the eyeballs again. They are how the particle eyes find the sockets. Be aware they sit parked at the armature origin at runtime, so eyeball meshes weighted to them may collapse to a single point — check that in the test page before relying on it.
  3. Morph normals off. They double the morph data and buy nothing here: the targets carry positions only, so shading inside an open mouth is slightly stale either way.
  4. Then check it. Load it in face-test.html, press mime, and watch the mouth run a sentence with no voice and no credits spent. The status line names which rig it picked and how many shapes it mapped.
